title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This typescript page is unrelated to the motivic Galois-theory notes on the neighbouring pages. It is upside down and probably reused paper (a verso). It belongs to the étale-descent material of SGA 4, Exposé VIII §9, on morphisms of universal effective descent for the category of étale sheaves. It finishes the proof of a statement numbered 9.4, which says that a surjective morphism f: X' → X is of universal effective descent for étale sheaves under several hypotheses a), b), c), d).

First paragraph (end of case c), presumably f flat and locally of finite presentation):
- Localize so that X is affine and there is an affine X'_1 → X that is of finite presentation, quasi-finite and faithfully flat, with a factorization through X'. This reduces to f quasi-finite.
- Localize further in the étale topology on X. By the local structure of quasi-finite morphisms (Zariski's Main Theorem, EGA IV 18.12), one finds an open X'_1 ⊂ X' with X'_1 → X finite and surjective.
- This reduces to case a), f finite surjective, already treated.

Section 9.4.4 (case d)):
- Localize to X a single point, then (using 1.1) to X = Spec k.
- Shrink X' to a nonempty affine open, so that f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
- Then f_* commutes with base change (to be shown later in the text).
- f is universally open (cited as EGA IV 2.4.9).
- So the hypotheses of 9.1 hold and the argument of 9.4.1 applies.

A handwritten addition reads: "ceci achève la démonstration de 9.4."
errors: No genuine error is visible. The claim that f_* commutes with every base change Y → Spec k is only announced ('comme nous verrons ultérieurement'). Its exact scope (which sheaves, which base changes) cannot be checked from this page alone.

The cited reference EGA IV 2.4.9 for universal openness cannot be verified here. Openness of flat morphisms locally of finite presentation is EGA IV 2.4.6; over a field, universal openness of any morphism is a separate result, possibly the one cited.

ideas.what: Reduction of descent for flat finite-presentation covers to quasi-finite and then finite surjective covers, via étale localization and Zariski's Main Theorem
ideas.modern_name: Universal effective descent for étale sheaves along fppf/finite surjective morphisms

ideas.what: Case where the base is the spectrum of a field: shrink to an affine open, use universal openness and base change for f_*, and apply criterion 9.1
ideas.modern_name: Universal effective descent for morphisms over a field

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 4 VIII descent theorem, reused as scrap paper in the motives file. It contains nothing new. The only curiosity is archival: its physical presence inside the motivic Galois notes.
transcription_corrections: The page is upside down in the scan; the transcription follows the correct orientation.
'et même contenu [?] de 1.1.' should most likely read 'et même compte tenu de 1.1.'
'X'_1 ⟶ X' (first paragraph) is the X-morphism X'_1 → X'; the second X'_1 is a different object, an open of X'.
Handwritten final line: 'ceci achève la démonstration de 9.4.'
